# `satl compose` { #satl-compose }

Deploy a Compose file on this node (use `satl stack` for the cluster).

`satl compose up` runs the whole file on the node you are talking to:
every service is pinned there with a node.id== constraint, ports are
published on that node rather than on the cluster's routing mesh, and a
relative bind or an `env_file` means a path on that node -- which is the
same machine as this client, since satl speaks a unix socket only. That
is `docker compose`'s scope. For `docker stack deploy`'s, spreading the
same file over the cluster on an overlay, use `satl stack deploy`.

What does not change between the two: every container is a task of a
service either way (there is no standalone container), so `up` creates
one service per compose service and `deploy:` is honoured rather than
ignored. Services are named <project>-<service> here and
<project>_<service> under `satl stack`, docker's own split; both answer
to the bare compose service name as a DNS alias, so the hostnames
inside the file keep working.

The project name comes from -p, else `COMPOSE_PROJECT_NAME`, else the
file's `name:`, else the directory; `down` removes exactly the objects
`up` labelled with it, and nothing else.

Anything outside the supported subset is refused with the file, the
service and the key named, never silently ignored. The subset and every
deviation are in docs/api-compat.md (entries 110-124, 169-174).

```console
$ satl compose [OPTIONS] <COMMAND>
```

`satl compose` is a group: it always takes one of the subcommands below.

**Options**

| Option | Description |
| --- | --- |
| <code>-f, --file &lt;FILE&gt;</code> | Compose file to read; found by walking up from the working directory when not given |
| <code>-p, --project-name &lt;NAME&gt;</code> | Project name (default: the project directory's name, normalized) |
| <code>--project-directory &lt;DIR&gt;</code> | Directory `env_file` paths and the default project name come from |

## `satl compose up` { #satl-compose-up }

Create or update the project's networks and services

```console
$ satl compose up [OPTIONS]
```

**Options**

| Option | Description |
| --- | --- |
| <code>-d, --detach</code> | Create everything and return, instead of attaching to the output |
| <code>-f, --file &lt;FILE&gt;</code> | Compose file to read; found by walking up from the working directory when not given |
| <code>-p, --project-name &lt;NAME&gt;</code> | Project name (default: the project directory's name, normalized) |
| <code>--remove-orphans</code> | Remove services of this project that the file no longer declares |
| <code>--project-directory &lt;DIR&gt;</code> | Directory `env_file` paths and the default project name come from |
| <code>--scale &lt;SERVICE=N&gt;</code> | Override a service's replica count: `--scale web=3`, repeatable |
| <code>--build</code> | Build the images of services that declare `build:` first |

## `satl compose down` { #satl-compose-down }

Remove the services and networks this project created

```console
$ satl compose down [OPTIONS]
```

**Options**

| Option | Description |
| --- | --- |
| <code>-f, --file &lt;FILE&gt;</code> | Compose file to read; found by walking up from the working directory when not given |
| <code>-v, --volumes</code> | Refused: see the message it prints |
| <code>-p, --project-name &lt;NAME&gt;</code> | Project name (default: the project directory's name, normalized) |
| <code>--remove-orphans</code> | Accepted for compatibility: `down` removes everything labelled with the project, so an orphan is removed either way |
| <code>--project-directory &lt;DIR&gt;</code> | Directory `env_file` paths and the default project name come from |

## `satl compose logs` { #satl-compose-logs }

Show the output of the project's tasks

```console
$ satl compose logs [OPTIONS] [SERVICE]...
```

**Arguments**

| Argument | Description |
| --- | --- |
| <code>[SERVICE]...</code> | Only these compose services (default: all of them) |

**Options**

| Option | Description |
| --- | --- |
| <code>-f, --file &lt;FILE&gt;</code> | Compose file to read; found by walking up from the working directory when not given |
| <code>--follow</code> | Follow log output.<br><br>Long-only, deliberately: `-f` is already `--file` at the `satl compose` level, where it is global so that every subcommand takes the same compose file, and one letter cannot mean two things. `satl logs -f` on a single container is unaffected (api-compat 179). |
| <code>-p, --project-name &lt;NAME&gt;</code> | Project name (default: the project directory's name, normalized) |
| <code>--tail &lt;N&gt;</code> | Number of lines to show from the end of each task's logs<br>Default: <code>all</code> |
| <code>--project-directory &lt;DIR&gt;</code> | Directory `env_file` paths and the default project name come from |
| <code>-t, --timestamps</code> | Show the daemon's timestamps |

## `satl compose build` { #satl-compose-build }

Build the images of services that declare `build:`

```console

```

| Argument | Description |
| --- | --- |
| <code>[SERVICE]...</code> | Only these compose services (default: every service with a `build:`) |

**Options**

| Option | Description |
| --- | --- |
| <code>-f, --file &lt;FILE&gt;</code> | Compose file to read; found by walking up from the working directory when not given |
| <code>--no-cache</code> | Re-execute every build step instead of reusing the cache |
| <code>-p, --project-name &lt;NAME&gt;</code> | Project name (default: the project directory's name, normalized) |
| <code>--project-directory &lt;DIR&gt;</code> | Directory `env_file` paths and the default project name come from |
